symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Number of endogenous variables.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of views.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Variable labels.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: View labels.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Pairs of views whose cross-covariance blocks are observed.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Observed view graph.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Generic first view label.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Generic second view label.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Generic source-variable label.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Generic target-variable or disturbance label.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Candidate next variable in a removal order.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Remaining variable distinct from a candidate next variable.

symbols.name: pi
symbols.def: Candidate common topological order \(\pi=(\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(p))\).

symbols.name: pi0
symbols.def: A common topological order of the data-generating mechanism.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Centered view vectors \(X=(X^{(a)}:a\in M)\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Joint law of \(X\).

symbols.name: B0
symbols.def: Data-generating structural coefficients \(B^0=(B^{0,(a)}:a\in M)\).

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.def: Structural disturbances \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon^{(a)}:a\in M)\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: For \(j\in V\), \(\Gamma_j=\operatorname{Cov}_P((\varepsilon_j^{(a)})_{a\in M})\).

symbols.name: M_CA
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) is the component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class in \(\text{def:component-aligned-limvam-class}\).

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.def: \(\Sigma^{ab}=\operatorname{Cov}_P(X^{(a)},X^{(b)})\), with \(\Sigma^{ba}=(\Sigma^{ab})^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: O_G
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_G=((\Sigma^{aa})_{a\in M},(\Sigma^{ab})_{\{a,b\}\in E})\).

symbols.name: B_pi
symbols.def: \(B_\pi=(B_\pi^{(a)}:a\in M)\) is the marginal modified-Cholesky regression family.

symbols.name: R_pi
symbols.def: \(R_\pi^{ab}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}\) on diagonal blocks and edges of \(G\).

symbols.name: Q_pi
symbols.def: \(Q_{\pi,j}\) retains \(R_\pi^{aa}[j,j]\) and \(R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]\) on the diagonal and edges of \(G\).

symbols.name: Pi_G
symbols.def: \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\) is the set of model-compatible common orders.

symbols.name: Theta_G
symbols.def: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\}\) with numerical duplicates removed.

symbols.name: N_out
symbols.def: \(N_{\mathrm{out}}=|\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)|\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Set of original variable labels already assigned coefficient rows.

symbols.name: U_A
symbols.def: Variables not yet removed at state \(A\).

symbols.name: Z_A
symbols.def: \(Z_A=(Z_A^{(a)}:a\in M)\) is the within-view residual family after projection on coordinates in \(A\).

symbols.name: C_A
symbols.def: \(C_A^{ab}=\operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_A^{(a)},Z_A^{(b)})\) on diagonal blocks and observed edges.

symbols.name: q_A
symbols.def: \(q^{ab}(A,r,t)\) is the observable cross-residual root score.

symbols.name: D_G
symbols.def: Removed-set compatibility graph built from the zero scores \(q_A\).

symbols.name: D_live
symbols.def: Source-to-sink pruning of \(\mathcal D_G\).

symbols.name: beta_A_r
symbols.def: \(\beta(A,r)=(\beta^{(a)}(A,r):a\in M)\) is the original-label regression row attached to transition \(A\to A\cup\{r\}\).

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho\) is a path from \(\varnothing\) to a live state \(A\) in \(\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\).

symbols.name: F_rho
symbols.def: \(F(\rho)\) stores the rows \(\beta(A',r')\) traversed by \(\rho\) in their immutable original row labels.

symbols.name: Comp_rho
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\) is the set of full numerical tuples obtained from live suffix paths extending \(\rho\).

symbols.name: H_A
symbols.def: \(H_A\) is the dictionary of distinct retained fragments at removed set \(A\).

symbols.name: Enum_G
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Enum}_G\) is the exact row-interning and integer-trie fragment traversal.
symbols.role: Recovery map for the coefficient-tuple estimand.

symbols.name: L_bits
symbols.def: Maximum binary encoding length of a rational entry of \(\mathcal O_G\).
symbols.role: Input-height parameter for the open bit-complexity question.

symbols.name: C_ER
symbols.def: Field operations and exact order or equality comparisons on real numbers each have unit cost.
symbols.role: Complexity model for the main theorem.

assumptions.condition: The law \(P\) of \(X\) is jointly centered Gaussian.

novel.justification: Full joint Gaussianity is a restrictive specialization beyond the base LiMVAM model. It is applicable to paired-sensor systems in which synchronized linear instruments are driven by jointly Gaussian coordinate shocks and Gaussian readout errors. The completion construction needs full joint Gaussianity because completed second moments then define a joint law and cross-coordinate zero covariances imply the independence required to assemble the coordinate disturbance blocks; neither implication is available from second moments alone for unrestricted non-Gaussian LiMVAM laws.

assumptions.condition: For every \(a\in M\), \(X^{(a)}=B^{0,(a)}X^{(a)}+\varepsilon^{(a)}\) almost surely under \(P\).
For every \(a\in M\), simultaneous row and column permutation by \(\pi_0\) makes \(B^{0,(a)}\) strictly lower triangular.
For distinct \(i,j\in V\) and all \(a,b\in M\), \(\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_i^{(a)},\varepsilon_j^{(b)})=0\).

novel.justification: The condition restricts cross-view dependence to disturbances carrying the same original variable label. It is satisfied by coordinate-aligned repeated sensors of the form \(\varepsilon_j^{(a)}=\lambda_{ja}U_j+\eta_j^{(a)}\), with independent coordinate shocks \(U_j\) and independent positive-variance readout errors \(\eta_j^{(a)}\). It is not asserted for unrestricted LiMVAM measurements.

Strict positive definiteness is natural when every repeated sensor has independent readout noise with positive variance in addition to any shared coordinate shock. It excludes singular common-noise boundaries and keeps the maintained model inside the positive-definite completion cone.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}=\{(P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0):p\ge2,\ m\ge2,\ (P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\text{ satisfies every member property listed below}\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal O_G\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_G=((\Sigma^{aa})_{a\in M},(\Sigma^{ab})_{\{a,b\}\in E})\), where \(\Sigma^{ba}=(\Sigma^{ab})^{\mathsf T}\) and no nonedge cross-block is observed.

definitions.name: \(B_\pi\)
definitions.construction: For each \(a\in M\), \(k\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and \(A_{k-1}=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k-1)\}\), set \(B_\pi^{(a)}[\pi(k),A_{k-1}]=\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),A_{k-1}]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},A_{k-1}]\}^{-1}\), set all other entries of that row to zero, and set \(L_\pi^{(a)}=I_p-B_\pi^{(a)}\).

definitions.name: \(R_\pi\)
definitions.construction: For every \(a\in M\) and every \(\{a,b\}\in E\), set \(R_\pi^{aa}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}\) and \(R_\pi^{ab}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: \(Q_{\pi,j}\)
definitions.construction: For each \(j\in V\), define the partial symmetric \(m\times m\) matrix \(Q_{\pi,j}\) by \(Q_{\pi,j}[a,a]=R_\pi^{aa}[j,j]\) for \(a\in M\) and \(Q_{\pi,j}[a,b]=R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]\) for \(\{a,b\}\in E\); nonedge entries are unspecified.

definitions.name: \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{\pi\in\mathfrak S_V:\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0\text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E,\text{ and every }Q_{\pi,j}\text{ admits a completion in }\mathbb S_{++}^m\}\).

definitions.name: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi=(B_\pi^{(a)})_{a\in M}:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\}\), where set braces remove numerical duplicates, and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}=|\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)|\).

definitions.name: \(Z_A,C_A\)
definitions.construction: For every \(A\subseteq V\) and \(U_A=V\setminus A\), set \(Z_A^{(a)}=X_{U_A}^{(a)}-\Sigma^{aa}[U_A,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}X_A^{(a)}\), with the second term zero when \(A=\varnothing\), and set \(C_A^{ab}=\operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_A^{(a)},Z_A^{(b)})\) for diagonal blocks and \(\{a,b\}\in E\).

definitions.name: \(q^{ab}(A,r,t)\)
definitions.construction: For \(A\subseteq V\), \(r,t\in U_A\), \(r\ne t\), and both orientations of every \(\{a,b\}\in E\), define \(q^{ab}(A,r,t)=C_A^{ab}[r,t]-C_A^{ab}[r,r]C_A^{bb}[r,r]^{-1}C_A^{bb}[r,t]\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal D_G\)
definitions.construction: Create every subset vertex \(A\subseteq V\) and the edge \(A\to A\cup\{r\}\), \(r\in U_A\), exactly when \(q^{ab}(A,r,t)=0\) for all \(t\in U_A\setminus\{r\}\) and both orientations of every \(\{a,b\}\in E\); obtain \(\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\) by retaining exactly vertices reachable from \(\varnothing\) that can reach \(V\).

definitions.name: \(\beta(A,r)\)
definitions.construction: For every \(A\subseteq V\), \(r\in V\setminus A\), and \(a\in M\), set \(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)[A]=\Sigma^{aa}[r,A]\{\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\}^{-1}\) and \(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)[V\setminus A]=0\), with the whole row zero when \(A=\varnothing\); collect these viewwise rows as \(\beta(A,r)\).

definitions.name: \(F(\rho),\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\)
definitions.construction: For a live prefix \(\rho=(\varnothing=A_0\to A_1\to\cdots\to A_k=A)\), where \(A_s=A_{s-1}\cup\{r_s\}\), define \(F(\rho)\) by placing \(\beta(A_{s-1},r_s)\) in original row slot \(r_s\) for \(s=1,\ldots,k\) and leaving other slots unassigned; define \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\{T_\pi:\pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path of }\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\text{ extending }\rho\}\).

definitions.name: \(\operatorname{Enum}_G\)
definitions.construction: Precompute \(\beta(A,r)\) on live edges; separately for each original row label sort these finite exact-real rows lexicographically and intern equal rows as one integer identifier; set \(H_{\varnothing}=\{F_{\varnothing}\}\); process live subsets by cardinality and, for every \(F\in H_A\) and live edge \(A\to A\cup\{r\}\), write the interned identifier of \(\beta(A,r)\) into slot \(r\) and insert the resulting integer vector into a deterministic binary trie for \(H_{A\cup\{r\}}\) only if absent; emit every decoded member of \(H_V\) once.

definitions.name: Fraction-free immutable-row handle
definitions.construction: Represent each principal regression solve defining \(\beta(A,r)\) by Gauss--Bareiss exact division on the corresponding integer-scaled augmented covariance matrix, retain determinant minors as equality certificates for row interning, and propagate only canonical integer certificate identifiers through the fragment tries.

statements.statement: Let \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), and suppose the predecessor set of \(r\) under \(\pi\) is exactly \(A\). Then the original-label row \(B_\pi^{(a)}[r,\cdot]\) equals \(\beta^{(a)}(A,r)\) for every \(a\in M\). Hence that row is invariant to the order within \(A\) and to every suffix after \(r\).
statements.justification: The immutable row is the model-specific write-once label that replaces the failed completed-path quotient.
statements.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Appendix D.3, preserves the residual LiMVAM after removing a recovered root, but it does not express every orderwise structural row as a function of its original-label predecessor set for quotient enumeration.
statements.consumer: A duplicate-free calibration solver can cache a row once and never replay the removal history that produced it.

statements.statement: Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and let \(\mathcal O_G\) be its observed moments for an arbitrary view graph \(G\). A permutation \(\pi\) is a source-to-sink path in \(\mathcal D_G\) if and only if \(\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\). For every such path, each \(Q_{\pi,j}\) has a positive-definite completion obtained as a coordinate principal block of a full residual covariance, and independently assembling these completed blocks yields a component-aligned Gaussian completion with coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\).
statements.justification: This closes the only load-bearing model-specific composition boundary between observable recursive tests and globally valid arbitrary-pairing completions.
statements.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3, treats fully paired recursive identification, while GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion, Theorem 7, characterizes chordal completion patterns. Neither composes an arbitrary view-graph root path with coordinatewise positive-definite noise completion on maintained LiMVAM inputs.
statements.consumer: Analysts with only selected paired view cohorts obtain an exact population certificate that every emitted coefficient tuple belongs to a full component-aligned mechanism.

statements.statement: Let \(\rho\) and \(\rho'\) be live prefixes ending at the same removed set \(A\). Then \(F(\rho)=F(\rho')\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)=\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')\). Moreover, if \(F(\rho)\ne F(\rho')\), then \(\operatorname{Comp}(\rho)\cap\operatorname{Comp}(\rho')=\varnothing\), and the legal suffix paths depend only on \(A\).
statements.justification: Right congruence makes fragment merging complete rather than a heuristic numerical deduplication at the sink.
statements.gap: WangEtAl2023EquivalenceClasses, Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, proves polynomial-delay quotient enumeration for local colors in decomposable acyclic AND--OR graphs. LiMVAM tuple equality is covariance-dependent and can be exposed only by later rows, so the required congruence must be proved from immutable original-label projections after source-to-sink pruning.
statements.consumer: A calibration frontier can merge factorially many commuting root orders without losing or duplicating a future coefficient mechanism.

statements.statement: For every \(A\subseteq V\), each retained fragment in \(H_A\) is the projection onto rows indexed by \(A\) of at least one tuple in \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\), distinct fragments at \(A\) project to disjoint nonempty output subsets, and therefore \(|H_A|\le N_{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\sum_{A\subseteq V}|H_A|\le2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the number of attempted fragment transitions is at most \(p2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}\).
statements.justification: The projection charge converts a compact state representation into a total cost controlled by numerical outputs rather than compatible orders.
statements.gap: WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 4, gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration for graph-distinct outputs, and DeepHuKoutris2021ProjectedEnumeration, Theorem 7, gives output-dependent delay for projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing. Neither bounds numerical coefficient fragments in a causal removed-set DAG by the final tuple count.
statements.consumer: Sparse or degenerate LiMVAM systems with many compatible orders but few coefficient tuples avoid factorial intermediate storage.

statements.statement: Under the premises of \(\text{thm:qpath-completion-exactness}\), \(\operatorname{Enum}_G(\mathcal O_G)\) emits exactly \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\), each numerical tuple once. In the ordered exact-real model \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ER}}\), deterministic construction and pruning of \(\mathcal D_G\), exact lexicographic row interning, integer-fragment trie propagation, decoding, and output require \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) total time and space; an explicit time bound is \(O((m+|E|)p^3 2^p+p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}+mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}})\). No hash oracle on real numbers and no traversal of all compatible orders is used.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies the exact-once, output-sensitive numerical frontier that the parent calibration proposal lacked.
statements.gap: GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, Theorem 3, minimally partitions MPDAGs by distinct total-effect functionals. WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 1, establishes AMO enumeration; Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration; Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs; and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. None enumerates covariance-dependent LiMVAM coefficient tuples from a \(2^p\)-state recursive representation with cost controlled by the number of distinct numerical outputs.
statements.consumer: The PairwiseLiMVAM and DirectLiMVAM workflow can report every population coefficient mechanism licensed by partial pairing before applying the inherited covariance-region inference to sampling uncertainty.

statements.statement: If \(B^{0,(a)}=0\) for every \(a\in M\), then every compatible order induces the same zero tuple. For an empty observed view graph, all \(p!\) orders are compatible, \(N_{\mathrm{out}}=1\), and the fragment algorithm retains exactly one fragment in every subset bucket \(H_A\), hence \(2^p\) fragments in total.
statements.justification: The reduction verifies that the claimed quotient removes genuine factorial order multiplicity in the standard no-edge special case.
statements.gap: Ordinary linear-extension and DAG enumeration methods still list structural witnesses in this case; the proposition records the required collapse to one numerical mechanism.
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain a boundary regression test that detects accidental order enumeration or failure to intern identical zero rows.

statements.statement: For rational \(\mathcal O_G\) of entry height at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\), use the fraction-free immutable-row handle to determine whether exact-once enumeration admits total bit complexity polynomial in \(p,m,L_{\mathrm{bits}},2^p,N_{\mathrm{out}}\) and the emitted encoding length, including canonical equality certificates for interned rows; if not, identify a family forcing superpolynomial intermediate or certificate growth.
statements.justification: The ordered exact-real theorem does not determine whether exact rational implementations remain output-polynomial in the ordinary Turing model.
statements.gap: Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity controls integer growth in one fraction-free elimination, but no located result controls simultaneous principal-regression keys, exact row equality certificates, and fragment tries over all \(2^p\) LiMVAM states.
statements.consumer: Exact symbolic causal-discovery software needs a certified representation bound before the population enumerator can be advertised as polynomial-bit rather than unit-cost exact-real.

sampling_model.design: The identification kernel takes exact population covariances on an arbitrary fixed view graph \(G\). The inherited inference layer may use one sourcewise independent and identically distributed paired sample for each observed edge together with every view-marginal sample.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment variable; the causal target is the finite set of shared-order structural coefficient tuples.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. Full joint Gaussianity, component alignment, one target population, and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances are maintained. The Gaussian specialization is applicable to synchronized linear sensors driven by jointly Gaussian coordinate shocks and Gaussian readout errors; unrestricted LiMVAM laws, selection, transport, and arbitrary off-model covariance arrays are excluded.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The new theorem is population-computational. Sampling uncertainty is handled only by the parent covariance-region inversion over empirical edge and marginal covariance blocks; no new rate, limit law, or continuum-region enumerator is claimed.

target_estimand: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\}\), with numerical duplicates removed

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3 identify the shared causal partial order and view-specific coefficient matrices by recursively recovering roots and preserving the residual LiMVAM under the paper's second-order diversity condition; the paper does not impose the full joint Gaussianity added by the present specialization.
Theorem 7 states that every partial positive-definite matrix with a fixed sparsity graph has a positive-definite completion exactly when the graph is chordal.
Theorem 3 shows that IDGraphs partitions the DAGs represented by an MPDAG into subclasses with identified, pairwise distinct total-effect functionals.

Theorem 1 establishes AMO enumeration, Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration, Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs, and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization.

Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives a framework that enumerates equivalence classes represented by local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph with polynomial delay.
Theorem 7 gives an output-dependent delay bound after linear preprocessing for projected star-query enumeration by heavy-light partitioning and interleaving.
Reverse search enumerates a connected family from a locally computable parent map without retaining a global visited set.
Fraction-free Gaussian elimination uses exact divisibility from Sylvester's identity to prevent the exponential intermediate growth of naive fraction-producing elimination.

tldr: Many common orders can encode the same coefficient tuple in the restrictive component-aligned, jointly Gaussian LiMVAM subclass, so traversing every compatible order can be factorial even when the causal output is a singleton. This specialization covers paired-sensor systems driven by jointly Gaussian coordinate shocks and Gaussian readout errors; it does not cover unrestricted LiMVAM laws. The population algorithm labels each removed-set transition by the immutable original-label regression row \(\beta(A,r)=\Sigma[r,A]\Sigma[A,A]^{-1}\), prunes dead subset states, interns exact rows, and merges equal live fragments. The central claims establish arbitrary-view-graph path exactness with positive-definite coordinate-noise completion, prove that live-fragment equality is exactly a right congruence for numerical completions, charge each fragment bucket to the final tuple set, and enumerate \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) exactly once in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space.

project_justification.gap: The parent calibration frontier has a \(2^p\)-state compatibility graph but no noncircular way to enumerate distinct numerical tuples without traversing all compatible paths. Published causal enumeration partitions graph classes by graphical effect formulas or lists graph-distinct DAGs, while general quotient enumeration assumes local decomposability not established for covariance-dependent coefficient equality.
project_justification.niche: At a fixed removed set \(A\), every future compatibility test depends only on the Schur residual state, and the row assigned when \(r\) is removed is the immutable original-label regression \(\beta(A,r)\). After source-to-sink pruning, the resulting fragments have nonempty, either identical or disjoint, completion sets.
project_justification.fill: Exact row interning and deterministic integer tries implement the fragment quotient without a real hash oracle. The projection lemma bounds every subset bucket by \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the maintained-model completion theorem certifies that each sink is a genuine arbitrary-pairing component-aligned Gaussian mechanism. Joint Gaussianity is an additional restrictive specialization that makes the coordinatewise covariance completion a valid joint disturbance-law construction.

related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3, supplies the shared-order recursive-residual model and the orderwise coefficient regressions; it does not impose the full joint Gaussian law used here and does not enumerate the numerical equivalence class left by partial pairing. Joint Gaussianity is therefore an additional restrictive specialization of the present component-aligned model, not a condition attributed to the base LiMVAM model. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, Theorems 2--3, motivates quotienting structural representatives by the causal output, but its recursive signatures are graphical total-effect functionals rather than covariance-dependent coefficient rows. WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 1, establishes AMO enumeration; Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration; Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs; and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. Those graph-distinct output counts can remain factorial when many orders share one numerical tuple. WangEtAl2023EquivalenceClasses, Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives the nearest general quotient framework, but its proof relies on local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph; the present right congruence is instead derived from immutable numerical row projections and live-prefix pruning. DeepHuKoutris2021ProjectedEnumeration, Theorem 7, gives output-dependent delay for projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing, demonstrating that projection changes enumeration complexity and that output-sensitive charging can be decisive without treating causal coefficient fibers. GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the completion boundary for chordal sparsity patterns; the model-specific step here uses a generating full covariance as a certificate for any arbitrary view graph on maintained inputs. AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch provides an alternative exact enumeration paradigm but requires a locally searchable parent relation that numerical tuple classes do not supply. Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity informs the open rational bit-complexity direction, not the ordered exact-real theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The total-cost theorem is stated in an ordered exact-real model and does not imply polynomial bit complexity or floating-point stability. It gives a \(2^p\)-state-plus-output bound, not polynomial delay and not a polynomial-in-\(p\) algorithm. The q-only graph construction is valid for moment collections generated by the maintained component-aligned jointly Gaussian model; an arbitrary off-model nonchordal edge array may pass every local q-test while admitting no positive-semidefinite completion. Exact enumeration over a continuum-valued covariance confidence region is not claimed. The generic write-once dynamic-programming lemma, row sorting, and integer tries are implementation machinery rather than independent causal contributions.
honest_scope: The contribution is confined to exact population enumeration of the coefficient-tuple frontier for the component-aligned, jointly Gaussian LiMVAM subclass under an arbitrary fixed pairing graph. Full joint Gaussianity is an added restrictive specialization rather than a feature of unrestricted LiMVAM; it is credible for paired-sensor Gaussian regimes and is required here so covariance completion defines the joint disturbance law and converts cross-coordinate orthogonality into independence. A shared order, component alignment, and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances are also maintained. The parent covariance-region inversion is reused only as the uncertainty layer after population identification; no new inferential theorem is asserted. Formal proof work must close the composition from q-path residual diagonality to independently assembled coordinate-noise completions. The all-zero empty-graph reduction must collapse \(p!\) orders to one tuple. Rational bit complexity remains an explicit open-ended question.

literature_map: Heurtebise et al. introduce LiMVAM, identify shared causal partial orders and coefficients by second-order diversity, prove recursive residual closure in Appendix D.3, and estimate coefficients by one-step feasible generalized least squares; the paper neither imposes the full joint Gaussian law added by the present restrictive specialization nor enumerates the numerical ambiguity left by partial pairing. Guo and Perkovi\'c, Theorems 2--3, recursively partition an MPDAG into subclasses with pairwise distinct total-effect functionals, furnishing the writing arc from repeated structural witnesses to minimal causal outputs. Wien\"obst et al., Algorithm 1 and Lemma 3, use maximum-cardinality-search structure and branch disjointness; Theorem 1 establishes AMO enumeration, Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration, Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs, and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. Wang et al., Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, enumerate locally colored equivalence classes in decomposable acyclic AND--OR graphs with polynomial delay, but their conclusion leaves nondecomposable quotient enumeration open. Deep, Hu, and Koutris, Theorem 7, use heavy-light partitioning and interleaving for output-dependent delay in projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing, confirming that projection can change the relevant output scale without supplying the LiMVAM congruence. Avis and Fukuda use locally searchable parent maps for memory-efficient reverse search. Conte et al. survey flashlight search, solution-graph traversal, push-out amortization, hardness, and approximation in output-sensitive graph enumeration; the fragment algorithm instead uses a model-specific right congruence and a direct projection charge. Grone et al., Theorem 7, give the chordal boundary for universal positive-definite completion; maintained component-aligned Gaussian inputs instead provide value-specific completions on arbitrary view graphs. Bareiss controls fraction-free elimination growth for one exact linear system, leaving aggregate row-key bit complexity open. Boege et al. provide adjacent algebraic Gaussian-DAG tools. Searches through September 7, 2026 found no closer paper that exact-once enumerates distinct LiMVAM coefficient tuples from a removed-set graph with total cost polynomial in \(2^p\) and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\).
novelty_justification: The closest causal-output comparator, GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, proves minimality for distinct graphical total-effect functionals, not equality of observed-covariance coefficient tuples. The closest graph enumerator, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, establishes AMO enumeration in Theorem 1; Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration; Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs; and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. These graph-distinct routines cannot exploit factorial-to-one numerical collisions. The closest general quotient result, WangEtAl2023EquivalenceClasses, Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, requires a local colored decomposable AND--OR representation that the parent LiMVAM proposal did not have. The exact delta is the model-specific proof that \(\beta(A,r)=\Sigma[r,A]\Sigma[A,A]^{-1}\) is a write-once original-label row, that equality of live fragments at fixed \(A\) is an if-and-only-if right congruence with disjoint unequal completion sets, and that every fragment bucket injects into the final distinct tuple set. Combined with arbitrary-view maintained-input completion exactness, this yields exact-once enumeration in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space. An independent rational exhaustive check passed seven \(p\le4\) cases, including complete, empty, path, and nonchordal cycle pairing graphs, and verified every prefix-completion equivalence, disjointness claim, sink set, and bucket bound; this is feasibility evidence rather than proof.
